To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a lowland rain forest type of vegetation, with a high proportion of angiosperm pollen, existed in Ethiopia in the Late Miocene.

the pollen/spore flora and the clay mineralogy of a late Miocene lake-beds in the Ethiopian Highlands show that the climate was warm and humid, and that the vegetation was dominated by lowland rainforest, which is not in line with the global cooling and aridification that took place in the late Miocene.

the pollen and clay mineral assembles from Chilga, a late Miocene lacustrine deposit on the Northwestern Ethiopian Highlands, indicate a rainforest vegetation that was not affected by the global cooling and the aridification that occurred in the Mediterranean and the equatorial zones at the end of the Cenozoic.

a unique palynological and mineralogical record from a Late Miocene sequence in Ethiopia.
the palaeobotanical and palaeoclimatic evolution of the Ethiopian highlands, and the palaeoecological implications of this study are discussed.

the reconstruction of the Late Miocene palaeoenvironmental conditions in the Chilga area of northwestern Ethiopia, based on the study of the pollen and spore flora, the clay mineral assembles, and the sedimentary environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pollen flora of Chilga is a relict of the Miocene rainforest of East Africa, which was replaced by savanna-type vegetation during the Late Miocene.
the Chilga flora is the oldest and most complete record of lowland rain forest vegetation from East Africa and the only one from the Ethiopian highlands.
the Chilga flora represents the last remnants of the humid, lowland rainforest vegetation that once covered most of the Ethiopian highlands during the Late Cenozic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a humid and warm climate, which is not necessarily related to the presence of the African Equator, was the most favourable factor for the development of lowland rainforests in East Africa.
the Chilga pollen assemblages indicate a warm and humid climatic regime in the Late Miocene of the Ethiopian highlands, with a vegetation cover dominated by a lowland rainforests.
the pollen flora from the Chilga lacustrine deposit is a unique one and is the first record of a humid lowland rainforest in the Ethiopian region since the end of the Eocene.
